prompt: Vertical frame of a deserted recreation ground at the very end of a hot summer day, roughly 1999: knee-high meadow grass gone gold and feathery fills the bottom third, and half hidden in it lies a small kid's BMX dropped on its side, handlebars twisted, one pedal pointing at the sky. Behind it the field runs flat to a thin dark strip of oak trees and a single wooden bench, tiny and far away, and that low horizon sits well below the middle of the picture. The upper half is pure open sky, a smooth wash that starts as warm peach just above the trees and cools upward into a faded powder blue, empty of clouds, birds, wires and aircraft. The camera is a family handycam propped on a garden wall at adult eye level, left recording and untouched, framed straight and level, focus drifting slightly soft. The image has the gentle smeary quality of a tape transfer from a home video compilation: colours slightly bleached and rosy, the peach glowing and bleeding a touch into the tree line, a fine fizz of chroma speckle in the darkening grass, faint horizontal wobble near the bottom edge, highlights soft and milky. Mood: hushed, warm and a little heartbreaking, the moment after the last kid has been shouted home and the tape keeps rolling over nothing. The picture is clean of any writing, numbers, overlays or graphics.
